Drama / Thriller · 15 min

01 — The pitch

A romantic getaway with nowhere to run.

When love
becomes a trap.

Rose and Matt’s marriage is on the rocks. In a desperate attempt to save the relationship, Matt takes Rose deep into the wilderness for a weekend camping trip. Alone together, it quickly starts to feel more like a trap than a romantic weekend getaway.

Then Rose gets separated from Matt. As night closes in and she desperately tries to find shelter, a terrifying thought begins to take hold: What if Matt left her here on purpose?

03 — The crew

So far

Shot by Jonathan Michael Mahoney.

Our film will be lensed by the brilliant Jonathan Michael Mahoney. Jonathan has shot features, shorts, commercials, music videos and experimental films. A graduate of CalArts and FAMU in Prague, he specializes in 35mm cinematography.

Most recently, Jonathan worked as a camera operator on Avatar: Fire and Ash. He was selected by Kodak as an official 16mm film-stock tester for Vision3 250D before its commercial release, and is excited to shoot 16mm again.

“Film is intention.

04 — The film

Literally

We’re shooting on 16mm film.

Shooting on film will cost about $1,000 more than shooting digitally. The results will be worth every penny.

Film is intention. Film is a magic trick. A literal illusion. In the wilderness, it means rich greens in the trees, texture in the skin, and the unmistakable grain of 16mm.

Read Ben’s extended love letter to film ↓
Ben’s extended love letter to film

When I was in film school making my first short films, shooting on actual film seemed to be my good luck charm. These were invariably my best works compared with most of what I shot digitally. Film is precious and therefore demands precision. It brings a different level of focus to the set.

Digital became the default, thought of as a cheaper option than film. I still believe that film at its best is consistently better than digital at its best. And in the wilderness? I want to see the rich greens of the trees and the texture of skin through the grain of 16mm.

Have I mentioned I love film? You’re gonna love the way it looks. I guarantee it.

05 — The ask

Every contribution counts

Help us make the film.

Our goal is to raise $20,000 to make and distribute Fell Out Of Love. We’re planning to shoot in mid-January in the greater Los Angeles area, with an aim to reach our goal by November 15.

No amount is too big or too small. Every donor will be credited onscreen by name, and more resources mean more can go up on the screen.
